titleStmt.title: TEI P5 version 4.12.0 and Stylesheets version 7.61.0 release notes

sourceDesc.p: Created retrospectively from ChangeLog and GitHub trackers

body.p: Release 4.12.0 is codenamed The Igor Release, because 203 years ago, July 28, 1823 marked the theatrical debut of Victor Frankenstein’s lab assistant (then named Fritz but better known to us today as Igor) in the very first stage adaptation of the novel Frankenstein. Coincidentally this release introduces new encoding for theatrical performance data.

The release includes other revisions to the TEI Guidelines, and it resolves a number of issues. Several of these changes and corrections are a consequence of feature requests or bugs reported by the TEI community using the GitHub tracking system. A full list of the issues resolved in the course of this release cycle may be found under the 4.12.0 milestone. Many thanks to the community contributors who reported issues, sent bug fixes, and helped with the drafting that led to this release, including: Julia J. Beine, Lou Burnard, James Cummings, Gabriel Egan, Frederik Elwert, Dario Kampkaspar, Jun Ogawa, Kazuhiro Okada, Klaus Rettinghaus. We are especially grateful to Peter Stadler for helping prepare and monitor new server infrastructure for this release.

The following changes are particularly worth highlighting in this release:
New encoding features
The teidata.point datatype now allows an optional third coordinate to support the encoding of surfaces and zones on three-dimensional objects, with new explanation and examples in the Guidelines (#2816, PR #2821, and PR #2922).
We introduce interleave to simplify content modeling in ODD. With this release, interleave is now the preferred way for ODD customizers to indicate unordered content models (where elements may appear in any order). Consequently, we deprecate the use of preserveOrder on the sequence element to indicate unordered content, and this attribute will no longer be valid on the sequence element after May 6, 2027. (See #2154 and PR #2538.)
Changes to content models and classes
Previously the perf atttribute was only available on the move and tech elements to encode performance-specific information. This release adds perf to a new att.performed to expand its use to actor and members of model.stageLike: camera, caption, move, sound, stage, tech, and view. (See #2724 and PR #2921.)
With this release, birth and death are now members of att.locatable, which permits applying the where attribute to these elements. Examples are provided to show how these can be used with linked data resources. (See #2873 PR #2923).

list.head: Revisions of prose and examples
list.item: A new paragraph has been added to the USE chapter to advise on use of the defaultExceptions attribute when introducing elements in other namespaces or no namespace in ODD customization (#2837 and PR #2928).
A broken link in the USE chapter has been corrected by pointing to a better resource in the TEI Vault (#2700 and PR #2934).

list.head: Housekeeping
list.item: Processing efficiency has been improved for building the TEI P5 Guidlines by revising an XPath comparison operator in p5odds.odd (#2926 and PR #2927).
